title: DHCPv4: Add support for option 162 Discovery of Network DNS resolvers

added 1 commit
  • 63386e5a - DHCPv4: Add support for option 162 Discovery of Network DNS resolvers
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22319/diffs?diff_id=1566252813&start_sha=37c563d13e42ffad13164ffa56be4674b6973a52)

It is misaligned relative to the above 3 and below 3 lines, but looking at the rest of the file it's not clear which one is the correct alignment. It seems most use the "left" alignment, but the "right" alignment would fit for all.
oh Yes... i will look later for fix
I'm guessing you mean "Addresses" and "dhcp.option.dnr.addresses"? I matched what done in DHCPv6 for DNR (using "address" and "dhcpv6.dnr.addrs"), but I can change both to match with the plural.

RFC 9463 uses "Addr length" for the length field, and then "IPv4 Address(es)" for DHCPv4 DNR (and "ipv6-address(es)" in DHCPv6 DNR), but for the whole block of data that corresponds to the address list. Since I add a protocol tree item for each address, shouldn't it remain as singular? Or, should I instead present it as a comma-separated list of the addresses in one protocol tree item instead?

So in the above screenshot, instead of

1 Address: 8.8.8.8

2 Address: 8.8.4.4

Should I do:

Addresses: 8.8.8.8,8.8.4.4
You can add item with all address (FT_NONE) and after each address (for filter)
